Remote aligner supervision and STL generation with dental monitoring®: Clinical integration and case report
academic.topic: Aligners, Clinical case management, SmartSTL & 3D models
academic.summary: Case report of a 23-year-old male with an anterior open bite treated with Spark aligners and buccal-shelf mini-screws, monitored with DentalMonitoring under custom protocols for aligner changes and hygiene. Of 59 scans, 88% were submitted on time; 16% showed a significant misfit (>0.5 mm), handled by extending wear 5 days and re-scanning or by clinician override; 36% triggered hygiene alerts with automated reinforcement messages. A remotely generated SmartSTL used for refinement planning superimposed accurately on a 3Shape intraoral scan. The authors report fewer in-office visits, high adherence and a light staff workload (hygienists ~10–15 min/day), with caveats: a single patient, relatively simple tooth movements, remote STL limited to Spark aligners and dependent on the patient's scanning skill. The lead author is a speaker for Ormco and DentalMonitoring.

academic.title: Dental Monitoring Application: it is a valid innovation in the Orthodontics Practice?
academic.summary: This clinical study evaluated the effectiveness of 0.014×0.025 CuNiTi wires in self-ligating orthodontic treatment over a 10-week period, monitored using the DentalMonitoring (DM) app. Thirty-five patients treated with the Damon System were scanned at baseline, 4, 8, and 10 weeks via DM. Results showed that the manufacturer’s estimated alignment time (≈8 weeks) underestimated real clinical efficiency. Using DM reduced in-office visits from three to two appointments over 10 weeks, leading to less chair time and lower material costs, while allowing more frequent and precise remote evaluations. Conclusion: Integrating DM with self-ligating systems enhances clinical efficiency and monitoring precision, offering measurable workflow benefits despite variability in patient compliance and sample size limitations.

academic.title: Effectiveness of AI-driven remote monitoring technology in improving oral hygiene during orthodontic treatment
academic.summary: A prospective clinical study evaluated the effectiveness of Dental Monitoring™'s AI-driven remote monitoring technology (AIDRM) in improving oral hygiene during braces orthodontic treatment. Two groups were studied: a DM Group (n=24) monitored weekly with personalized notifications, and a Control Group (n=25) not monitored by DM. Oral hygiene was assessed using the Orthodontic Plaque Index (OPI) and Modified Gingival Index (MGI). The DM Group was followed for 13 months, and the Control Group for 5 months. Statistical analysis involved independent Student's t-tests for inter-group comparisons and paired Student's t-tests for intra-group time point differences. Key findings showed that the DM group consistently had lower OPI and MGI values than the control group at all time points, with statistically significant differences observed at 5 months for both indices. While both groups experienced an initial rapid worsening of oral hygiene, AIDRM with weekly scans and personalized notifications appeared to mitigate this decline over time, though a long-term continuous improvement was not observed due to potential patient burnout and decreased compliance with scan completion

academic.title: The New Role of the Dental Assistant and Nurse in the Age of Advanced Artificial Intelligence in Telehealth Orthodontic Care with Dental Monitoring: Preliminary Report
academic.summary: The paper evaluates the benefits and drawbacks of daily automated assessments of orthodontic treatment progress, the impact of AI on personalized care, and the new role of a dental assistant. The paper concludes that AI will improve dental practice through more precise and personalized treatment, bringing new roles and responsibilities for trained medical professionals but raising new ethical and legal issues for dental practices.

academic.title: Pilot case control evaluation of artificial intelligence assisted orthodontic monitoring and pediatric patient perception
academic.topic: Aligners, Phase 1, Visits & chair time, Patient experience
academic.summary: This Pilot case-control evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted orthodontic monitoring using Dental Monitoring (DM) software in children treated with Invisalign First demonstrated significant benefits, particularly in clinical efficiency and patient satisfaction. Key Positives: Treatment Efficiency: The DM group (N=20) had a significantly lower number of appointments (mean 21.65 ± 4.51) compared to the control group (mean 31.58 ± 8.07), representing a substantial 68.56% reduction in visits. Undiminished Outcomes: DM achieved this reduction in appointments without negatively impacting key clinical metrics, as there were no significant differences in treatment duration or number of refinements between the groups. High Patient Satisfaction: Children monitored with DM reported highly favorable perceptions: 100% were satisfied or very satisfied with the DM application overall and with communication with the orthodontist. 85% found the scanning process very easy or easy. 85% would recommend the experience. 55% felt much calmer knowing they were continuously monitored.

academic.title: Accuracy of dentalmonitoring’s artificial intelligence in detecting aligner tracking issues: a retrospective multi-centric study
academic.summary: This multicenter retrospective comparative study evaluated the performance of DentalMonitoring artificial intelligence in detecting aligner tracking issues using 3,323 remote assessments from 623 orthodontic patients treated across multiple U.S. clinics. AI predictions were compared with a reference standard established through independent reviews by a panel of three orthodontic residents. Performance was assessed using both a binary model (seated vs. unseated aligner) and a three-level classification (seated, slight unseat, noticeable unseat). In the binary model, the AI achieved a sensitivity of 93.2% and specificity of 86.2%, with a positive predictive value of 89.2% and a negative predictive value of 94.4%. In the three-level model, detection of noticeable unseats showed a sensitivity of 91.1% and specificity of 90.5%, with a PPV of 66.1% and an NPV of 98.3%. The consistently high negative predictive values indicate strong reliability in ruling out clinically meaningful aligner misfit, suggesting that the system performs particularly well in minimizing false-negative assessments of unseated aligners.

academic.title: Accuracy of DentalMonitoring’s artificial intelligence in detecting common orthodontic braces treatment related emergencies
academic.summary: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of DentalMonitoring™ (DM) (Dental Monitoring SAS, Paris, France), an FDA-cleared AI-powered orthodontic remote monitoring software, in detecting three common orthodontic appliance issues: bracket debonding, open self-ligating clips, and tie loss. Datasets from 1,014 US-based patients were analyzed. Each DM image set was assessed by the AI algorithm and independently reviewed by a panel of three orthodontic experts, whose consensus served as the reference standard. A total of 659 evaluations were included for bracket debonding, 647 for self-ligating clip status, and 653 for tie presence. Sensitivity and specificity along with their 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a two-level evaluation basis (positive vs. negative) across the three clinical parameters. DM’s AI demonstrated high diagnostic performance, with sensitivity of 98.4% for bracket debonding, 91.1% for open self-ligating clips, and 93.3% for tie loss. Corresponding specificity values were 99.6%, 88.3%, and 96.5%, respectively. Current results indicate that DM’s AI analysis system has high accuracy in detecting bracket debonding, open self-ligating clips, and tie loss. DM can help significantly reduce the rate of these undetected clinical incidents, providing a better approach to managing emergencies and maintaining clinical control in orthodontic treatment.

academic.title: Characterizing orthodontic tooth movement in real time using dental monitoring scans: A pilot study
academic.summary: This prospective pilot study (n = 12) evaluated whether DentalMonitoring scans can track orthodontic tooth movement in short time intervals during maxillary canine retraction and assessed their accuracy compared with iTero scans. Patients submitted DM scans every 4–5 days over a 4–5 week period, and STL files were superimposed to measure tooth displacement in three spatial planes. Preliminary findings suggested that the greatest tooth movement occurred within the first few days after activation, followed by a slower constant rate. The study also reported promising agreement between DM photographic scans and intraoral scanner models, indicating that DM may enable near–real-time monitoring of orthodontic tooth movement. However, the small sample and pilot design limit the strength of conclusions.

academic.title: Assessment of AI-based monitoring method in assessing oral hygiene during orthodontic treatment
academic.summary: This prospective controlled clinical study (n = 40) evaluated whether AI-based remote monitoring with DentalMonitoring improves oral hygiene during orthodontic treatment. Patients were divided into a control group (standard care) and a test group using DM scans, and oral health was evaluated over 3 months using plaque index (OPI), gingival index (MGI), and white spot lesion assessments. The AI monitoring group showed significantly lower plaque accumulation, reduced gingival inflammation, and fewer white spot lesions compared with the control group. These findings suggest that remote monitoring may improve patient compliance and oral health during orthodontic treatment, although the small sample size and short follow-up limit the strength of the conclusions.

academic.title: AW passivity FDA paper
Quantitative evaluation of an artificial intelligence–driven remote monitoring system for occlusion assessment using patient-captured images
academic.summary: The evaluation of DM's AI model for remote orthodontic monitoring found high agreement with 3D reference standards for measuring midline deviation and overbite, with mean biases of -0.01 mm and -0.04 mm respectively. While overjet and canine classification also remained within clinically acceptable limits, they exhibited greater variability and modest directional biases, specifically a slight overestimation for overjet (+0.29 mm) and an underestimation for larger canine class deviations (-0.31 mm). These results indicate that while the AI model is highly accurate for specific parameters, its current performance variability for others suggests its most appropriate clinical role is for screening, triage, and follow-up rather than as a standalone diagnostic tool. Overall, the study supports the potential of AI-assisted image analysis for remote monitoring, provided that AI-generated measurements are interpreted alongside clinical judgment.

academic.title: SmartSTL FDA paper
Predicting Orthodontic Root Movements with the Dental Monitoring System: A Preliminary Study
academic.summary: This retrospective/observational study utilized records from 20 patients at two time points (T0 and T1) to evaluate the accuracy of Dental Monitoring’s (DM) SmartSTL model in predicting root movements, validating its performance against the Materialise 3-Matic software. The results demonstrated high accuracy in 3D reconstruction, with mean surface deviations between the SmartSTL and the control DMSTL models being extremely small (around 0.05 mm on both arches), and, crucially, the overall average difference in root movement between the DM and 3-Matic methods was not statistically significant. Based on these findings, the study concludes that the developed SmartSTL model may reliably predict root movements greater than 0.50 mm, suggesting a strong potential for integrating this technology into routine orthodontic monitoring once further refinements, such as high-quality scans and AI-assisted improvements, are implemented.

academic.title: Management of a Class III malocclusion combining MARPE with anterior nasomaxillary complex traction and clear aligners with telemonitoring support: Case report and workflow model
academic.topic: Phase 1, Aligners, Clinical case management, SmartSTL & 3D models
academic.summary: This study details a workflow model for managing late-adolescent Class III malocclusion using Miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) and anterior nasomaxillary complex traction followed by clear aligner therapy. A key component of the clinical management is the integration of AI-assisted telemonitoring (specifically Dental Monitoring®) to remotely supervise jackscrew activation, monitor soft-tissue status, and triage clear aligner progress through a rule-based GO/NO-GO protocol. The research highlights that telemonitoring enables effective remote supervision and potentially reduces in-office visits without compromising treatment safety or outcomes, provided there is strong patient adherence and a streamlined team workflow. Key performance indicators discussed include scan compliance, hygiene alerts for biofilm and gingivitis, and the accuracy of remote STL capture for refinement planning

academic.title: Evaluating the Artificial Intelligence Driven Monitoring System Notifications: Clear Aligner and Oral Hygiene Perspectives
academic.topic: Aligners, AI accuracy, Oral hygiene & perio
academic.summary: This study (23 clear aligner patients, 533–1,425 observations per parameter) evaluates the validity of DentalMonitoring's AI notification software against an orthodontist's visual review of the same scans. The AI shows high accuracy (>90%) for generalized detection (presence or absence) of clear aligner and oral hygiene issues, but accuracy drops for localized detection (identifying the exact tooth). For example, a "slight unseat" has a localized accuracy of 54.2%, and "slight plaque/food" 49.7%. The authors conclude DM is a viable clinical aid but is not fully automated and needs close oversight by the orthodontist.

academic.title: Randomized controlled trial comparing AI-assisted digital and conventional orthodontics: Superior PAR reduction and occlusal outcomes
academic.summary: In a single-center randomized controlled trial, 140 patients with Angle Class I malocclusion were evaluated to compare an AI-assisted digital workflow (incorporating DentalMonitoring, 3Shape Ortho Analyzer, and TRIOS 4 scanning) against conventional fixed-appliance therapy. The methodology utilized a parallel-group design where the digital group received clinician-directed care augmented by automated tooth segmentation, 3D-printed custom brackets, and algorithm-guided remote monitoring. Key findings revealed that the AI-assisted group achieved significantly superior occlusal outcomes, with a mean post-treatment Peer Assessment Rating (PAR) score of 4.88 compared to 7.81 in the conventional group. Furthermore, a much higher proportion of patients in the AI-assisted group reached the "greatly improved" threshold (≥70% PAR reduction) at a rate of 82.9% versus 50.0% for the conventional group. While these results demonstrate improved short-term occlusal quality, the study noted that the benefits reflect the integrated digital system rather than isolated AI effects.

academic.title: Tooth-level spatial distribution of AI-detected oral hygiene insufficiency in fixed appliance versus clear aligner patients: A large-scale analysis using the dental monitoring™ platform.
academic.journal: Journal of the World federation of orthodontists
academic.summary: This large-scale retrospective study evaluated over 15.3 million AI-generated tooth-level scan notifications from 40,748 global orthodontic patients to analyze the spatial distribution of oral hygiene insufficiency between patients with fixed appliances (FA) and those undergoing clear aligner therapy (CAT). The key finding reveals that FA patients consistently carry a significantly higher oral hygiene burden than CAT patients, exhibiting worse mean insufficiency scores (0.85 vs. 0.55) across every single tooth, arch, tooth type, and quadrant. Both treatment groups demonstrated near-bilateral symmetry and a distinct spatial distribution where mandibular and anterior teeth—particularly canines and incisors—experienced the greatest hygiene burden. Notably, patient-level analysis indicated that this disparity is predominantly driven by a higher frequency of poor hygiene events among FA patients rather than a greater severity of plaque accumulation on already-affected teeth. Ultimately, these findings identify tooth-level targets for precision hygiene interventions, though authors note that substantial age imbalances between the two cohorts mean the appliance-type differences should be interpreted as associative

academic.title: The use of teleorthodontics and artificial intelligence for orthodontic triage and screening in a publicly funded healthcare system: A crossover randomized controlled trial
academic.summary: Single-centre crossover RCT in a Sydney public orthodontic clinic comparing triage by teleorthodontics with DentalMonitoring scans and AI against face-to-face screening. 255 referred patients were randomised and 178 completed both triages. For accepting or rejecting referrals (IOTN dental health component ≥3), the DM-based triage had a sensitivity of 1.0, specificity of 0.67 and overall accuracy of 0.98; three referrals were wrongly rejected. It was 2.9 times faster than face-to-face triage. The AI misread overbite/overjet in some patients and does not assess crossbite, contact-point displacement or functional shift. The authors conclude DM-based teleorthodontics is a valid and reliable screening tool for mild and severe malocclusions.
academic.limits: Single public clinic using IOTN; blinding not possible; AI misses several IOTN traits (crossbite, contact-point displacement, functional shift)
